description: Laravel package (lomkit/laravel-access-control) that declares in one control who can see and change each Eloquent model: its perimeters drive the policies, the query scopes and the Scout searches.
rules: These docs cover Laravel Access Control 1.x (lomkit/laravel-access-control), which requires PHP 8.3+ and Laravel 13. Laravel 12 applications stay on 0.7, the last 0.x release. Do not write 0.x code.
Install with composer require lomkit/laravel-access-control. There is no configuration file to publish: everything is declared in the controls.

Write one control per model in app/Access/Controls (php artisan make:control PostControl) with protected string $model and perimeters(); perimeter classes go in app/Access/Perimeters (php artisan make:perimeter ClientPerimeter).
Each perimeter declares allowed() (the permission, for an Ability), query() (its rows in SQL) and should() (one row in memory), or unrestricted(). query() and should() must describe the same rows.
Group perimeters with Levels::of(), widest first: only the highest level the user reaches applies. Keep tenants apart with a boundary() on the control.
Add the HasControl trait to the model and call Access::registerPolicies() in the boot() method of a service provider.

A query is controlled only when it says so: Post::query()->controlled()->paginate(), controlled('update') for another ability, Post::controlledFor($user) in jobs and commands. A controlled query without a signed-in user returns no row.
With Laravel Scout, use the ControlledSearchable trait, give each restricting perimeter searchKeys(), and end every search with controlled() or uncontrolled().
Run php artisan access:check in CI, and prove in tests with InteractsWithAccess (assertControlAgrees, assertLevelsNest, assertSearchAgrees) that the policy, the queries and the search agree.
